newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai man gets 13 years for using fake money.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai man gets 13 years for using fake money.

text.p: A Shanghai court has sentenced a local businessman to 13 years' jail and three others to terms of six months to four years for buying and using fake money, the Business News reported on Sunday.
The Hongkou District People's Court recently sentenced Wang Linsheng to 13 years and confiscated assets worth 100,000 yuan ($12,000), it said.
The other three received prison terms of six months, three years and four years and were fined 30,000, 50,000 and 60,000 yuan respectively, it said.

During six visits starting from September 1995, the four men bought fake money with a face value of nearly 60,000 yuan from a dealer in Putian, a city in the southeast province of Fujian, for about a third of that amount, it said.
They brought the fake money to Shanghai where they used it mainly at night to buy daily necessities, offering large notes to buy cheap items to get the change, it said.
The newspaper did not say who discovered the counterfeit notes and gave no more details.
